post.summary: Request a payout from a funded account
post.description:
Asks the broker to pay `amount` from a funded prop account to the person's client wallet.

Nothing moves until the broker approves it; the approve checks everything again.

`amount` is at most the payout available (the profit split of the REALIZED balance above the payout base, rounded down to cents), at least the program's `payout_min`, within the free margin, and must not take equity to the account's loss floors.

One open request per account, and a cooldown between payouts (`payout_cooldown_days`, counted from the funded start or the last paid payout).

Idempotent: send an `Idempotency-Key` header or `client_ref`; a retry with the same key and amount answers the first request with 200 and `"replayed": true`.

Fills immediately at the live feed price (BUY at the ask, SELL at the bid, plus the account group's spread markup), on the account's own leverage and terms.

HEDGING instances (paper, real) open a new position per fill; the response carries `position`.

NETTING instances (paper-net, real-net) apply the ticket to the symbol's single net position and add a `netting` block: action open | add | reduce | close | flip, remaining_qty, and closed_qty/realized_pnl when something closed; `position` is present unless the book went flat.

`reversed` lists the opposite positions a `reverse:true` ticket closed first.

Optional sl/tp attach brackets to the resulting position.

Margin is gated at fill ("insufficient free margin: required …, free …" → 400).

A suspended broker licence refuses openings (403); on netting a pure reduce is still allowed.

For an A-book member whose symbol the liquidity provider lists, the order goes to the LP: the answer is either the fill or `{success, pending:true, order_id, symbol, message}` when the LP has not answered yet.

Business refusals on our own books also save a REJECTED order (see EntryRefusal).

post.summary: Place a pending order (LIMIT / STOP / bracket)
post.description:
type LIMIT (needs `price` > 0) or STOP (needs `trigger_price` > 0) rests until the feed crosses it; already-marketable orders fill at once.

An A-book member's entry on `real`, on a symbol the liquidity provider lists, is sent there as a MARKET order when it triggers and fills at the provider's price (see Liquidity-provider execution).

Margin is gated when it triggers, not at placement: an entry that no longer fits is REJECTED with its brackets.

Optional p_sl/p_tp create dormant P_SL/P_TP children that become SL/TP when the entry fills. type SL / TP with parent_order_id = an open position's market_order_id attaches a bracket (one of each per position; a new level replaces the old); refused when it would trigger immediately. type P_SL / P_TP with parent_order_id = a PENDING LIMIT/STOP entry's order_id attaches a dormant bracket ("parent of a P_SL must be a PENDING LIMIT/STOP entry order").

For trigger types `price` doubles as trigger_price. oco_key (with algo_id) links entries one-cancels-other; trailing attaches a server trail to the entry (netting: only onto an empty net position).

On internal accounts with conversion_strict ON, conversion availability is checked when the entry triggers; missing conversion saves REJECTED with the same currency-conversion reason as market entry.

Pure netting reductions remain allowed.

get.description:
Upgrade to a WebSocket (wss://<host>/<slug>/v1/oms/<instance>/ws?token=<token>; browsers cannot set Authorization on a socket, so ?token= is accepted).

Server → client only: text frames, each one JSON object with an `event` field.

Client messages are read and ignored (the read loop only detects disconnect).

First frame: `{"event":"connected","heartbeat_ms":5000,"account_snapshots":<bool>,"snapshot_epoch":<n>}`.

Then `{"event":"heartbeat"}` every heartbeat_ms; treat a silence longer than that as a dead link and reconnect.

Protocol pings every 25 s (a missed pong closes the socket).

Events (fields vary by event; most carry `instance`): fill {order, position} — an entry filled; pending {order} — a pending order was placed; modify {order}; cancel {order_id, reason?, copied?}; reject {order_id, order, symbol, side, quantity, reason} — an entry refused (also margin rejects at trigger time); squareoff {position_id, realized_pnl}; reduce {position_id, realized_pnl, remaining_qty}; bracket_close {type, position_id, …} — an SL/TP/TSL closed a position; protection {position_id, trailing}; funds {funds} — a fresh Funds snapshot after any funds-moving event; basket {group_id, tag, legs, sl, tp}; group_trigger {type, group_id, …}; margin_call {active, margin_level, margin_call_level, stop_out_level?, equity, used_margin}; copy_skipped {master_order_id, …}; pamm_allocation, pamm_unfollow, mam_share; deposit_approved / deposit_rejected, withdrawal_<status>, kyc_<status> {reason}; lp_close_refused (A-book); account_snapshot (external venue accounts only).

Events without an `instance` field reach the member's sockets on every instance.

A connection that cannot keep up (more than 256 queued frames or 2 MB) is closed rather than left with a gap: on reconnect, refetch all_open.

The exact field set of the less common events is not enumerated here.

Deduplicate by alert.id and fetch /alerts/events on reconnect.

Email is best effort, at most one attempt per alert per 10 seconds.

Pending uncommitted detections are not crash-durable; bounded queue losses are logged and exposed in feed health.

The C++ edge forwards the raw upgrade over its existing Unix admission link; the engine performs atomic database redemption before account-binding and socket admission.

A replay/expired ticket alone gets 401.

Invalid tickets with a valid standing credential fall back to that credential.
